rationale: The workflow already implements the Gradle dependency-cache optimization supported by P-LIT-GHA-CACHE and the batch-interactive-three experiment: it uses actions/cache@v4 to cache ~/.gradle/caches and ~/.gradle/wrapper with a key derived from **/*.gradle* and gradle-wrapper.properties, plus restore-keys. The pattern's own contraindications list "An equivalent cache already exists," so re-applying it would be redundant and not a meaningful optimization. No other pattern's preconditions are satisfied: there is no matrix (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST), no scheduled runs (P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE, P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE), no Bazel build (P-LIT-BAZEL-*), no multiple configurations (P-LIT-CONFIG-REUSE), no representative successful-duration history for timeouts (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT, P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT), and no evidence supporting test/build selection or step skipping without risking required coverage.
